posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
I never do randomness.  I select heroes, and I'll play every hero eventually, but for the moment I'm putting the Argent Adept off for absolute last.  The music shtick bores me, and his playstyle seems irritatingly complicated.

Other than that, I have a mild dispreference for Wraith because her Equpment synergy is just too efficient to be exciting.  And playing Legacy isn't much fun; he's someone you want in your party, but you don't want to be stuck being the one who has to hold the pom-poms all game instead of actually doing anything.  (And has cards like Surge of Strength but hardly ever actually uses them because he doesn't really deal damage much.)  I put off Bunker and Fanatic for a fairly long time because the military and Christian themes didn't appeal to me, and I'm still a bit less likely to play Fanatic; Bunker on the other hand is just fun.  Tempest is on the verge of beginning to bore me as well.  Other than that, however, I just keep playing something different every time, and boredom is easily forestalled.

posts.name: awp832
posts.cooked:
It sort of depends,  often I'll go for long stretches without touching a particular hero and then go crazy with that same hero as I try to figure out either 1.  Why I didnt like them in the first place or 2.  New strategies that maybe I'll like them better.    Recently I was on a bit of a Nightmist-binge after practically not touching her since IR came out.   I've done the same thing for Absolute Zero and Mr. Fixer.

 

I play relatively few games as Expatriette.   Ammo cards are frusterating and she never seems to have what she needs.  Then as soon as she gets it, its Devestating Aroura and you're back to square 1.   Fixer is more or less in the same spot though I play him just slightly more I think.

 

Argent Adept is at the bottom of the pile for me though.  I'd rather play a hero that I feel is weak and fun like Mr. Fixer than one I find strong and a headache,  which is where AA fits in.   He's a good hero for sure,  but I really dont care to have to search through my deck AGAIN and grumble to myself  "freaking…  melody/rhythm… which freaking instrument are you?".    I'm also not  a fan of "Arcane Cadence!   …  reveal 5, one in my hand, one on top of my deck, one on bottom of my deck, one in the trash and play… Arcane Cadence!..    reveal 5, one in my hand, one on top of my deck…"   

 

Although,   even lower on the totem pole,  lower still that I actually forgot about him being a hero,  so low that he's not even in the box…   is the Scholar.   For much the same reasons I guess.   He just has to jump through way too many hoops.  And even more than that…   He has a cool factor of 0 to me.  I can't get into him.   He doesn't seem like a superhero.   He seems like if you took the Justice Leauge and decided you needed a new member and so you were going to add The Dude.     Don't get me wrong,  I love The Dude,  but I don't want him fighting crime alongside Batman and Flash.   He kills the entire theme of the game for me.

posts.name: byc
posts.cooked:
I tend to avoid long turn characters, although I love NightMist (and I play her really fast and without hesitation usually).  Having been on the receiving end of watching long turns, I try and avoid those.

I specifically avoid Tachyon because I think she's really really good, and it feels like easy mode when experienced players play her.

I specifically avoid Scholar because I feel like he does a lot of "nothing".  He sets up for..."nothing", unlike Absolute Zero/Bunker/ExPat who sets up powerful damage combos, Scholar feels like he just sits there.

I tend to avoid Fanatic unless Legacy is in the game because she gets shut down by damage reduction very easily.

I tend to avoid Legacy if my group has long turn characters.  Long turns by others just makes playing Legacy even harder as his decisions are often straightforward.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
I love duos in SotM, so I normally pick someone who pairs really well with another team member.

My least Favorites to play:

Legacy:  So powerful, so boring.

TLT:  I love Tachyon, Team Leader is like hitting the auto-win button and clapping, more to do than Legacy but feels the same anyway, that base power being so good, blech.

Nightmist:  She is not my style.  Even good games with her I dislike.

Wraith:  Really strong deck, has the single strongest card in the game (Impromptu Invention), but the goal is Utility Belt Micro and either razor/knives or double bolt every game.  I just don't find her fun unless the villain is really thwarting her.  She is a Hero I recommend to new players, she is great for learning the game, and my casual player friends tend to go back to her a lot.

Dark Visionary:  It's not a secret that Visionary is my favorite hero, but her dark side I just can't get into.  I think the whole base power of awesomeness is a big part, but also I love her original base power.  The worst thing in a card based game is getting a bad hand, Visionary is the solution to that, Dark Visionary I just keep thinking I could have helped our team more if I used the original.

 

Envisioner you sound like a Crono-Ranger fan in the making.
